item.title: Men's Group Gathers at Pilgrim Diner — Sat Nov 14, 8:30 AM
item.description:
In the Spring of 2026, parishioner Ken Traficante began an informal once-a-month gathering of men at Holy Spirit Verona. Having chaired the Building and Grounds (B&G) Committee for many years, Ken wanted to recreate the fellowship that would happen on B&G Work Day events when parishioners volunteered time to clean up and repair items around the Church's campus. Ken scheduled a Saturday morning once a month at the Pilgrim Diner in Cedar Grove with a group of 6-8 guys during which they would share conversation and life experience with one another. This breakfast group will now meet on the second Saturday of each month from 8:30 to 10am (unless otherwise indicated on the website calendar). For more information, speak with Father Jerry or Ken Traficante.
Source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

item.title: The Fall St. James Chamber Music Concert — Sun Nov 15, 4:00 PM — St. James Episcopal Church
item.description: St James Episcopal Church is excited to announce that this coming Sunday November 15th at 4PM it will host a chamber music concert featuring the renowned violinist Naoko Tanaka, along with 10 other esteemed musicians. Ms Tanaka will be performing “The Lark Ascending” by Ralph Vaughan Williams. Also on the program are works by Bach, Poulenc, Persichetti, Beethoven and Dvorak. Naoko Tanaka has given concert tours as a soloist and chamber musician in the U.S., South America, Europe, Asia and Canada. A former member of The Theater Chamber Players of The Kennedy Center and The Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, she is a current member of the New York Philomusica and serves as concert master of St Luke’s Chamber Ensemble. She is on the faculty at the Juilliard School, Brooklyn College Conservatory of Music, and The Aspen Music School during the summer. She has recorded for Deutsche Gramophone, Columbia Records, and Music Masters. St James Episcopal Church is at 581 Valley Road in Upper Montclair.

item.description:
Do you wish your clothes matched your gender and body type better? Does your wardrobe need an update? Join the LGBTQ+ Sewing Club! Learn basic sewing skills and update your clothes to match your identity and style. Not only is learning to sew a great life skill to have, but you will also be able to upcycle and restyle thrifted clothes and hand-me-downs. No prior sewing experience necessary! Bring a piece of clothing that you would like to upcycle. If you have a sewing machine or sewing needles and materials from home you want to use you are welcome to bring in and use during this session. You are also welcome to use a sewing machine in the studio. Allies are also welcome to join. A portion of the proceeds will be donated to Out Montclair. item.title: Flat Rock Brook Nature Center-Guest Speaker — Mon Nov 16, 2:10 PM — CELS 110
item.description:
Behind the Scenes of Nature Conservation! Ever wondered what it takes to run a nature center? Join the Environmental Club for a special guest speaker event featuring the Executive Director of Flat Rock Brook Nature Center in Englewood, NJ! Learn about the director’s leadership in environmental education, wildlife conservation, and protecting local ecosystems. Discover what goes into managing a nature preserve, the challenges of conservation, and exciting career opportunities in the environmental field. Don't miss this chance to hear firsthand experiences, ask questions, and get inspired to make a difference! Stephen Wiessner has served as Executive Director since 2006, bringing 20 years of leadership to Flat Rock Brook.
Hosted by: Environmental Club

item.title: Gettysburg: From the Aftermath to the Address — Mon Nov 16, 7:00 PM — Montclair Women’s Club
item.description: Victorian Society in America Northern New Jersey Chapter VSA-NNJ meets monthly from September to June for lectures and events related to 19th Century history, usually on the third Monday of the month. Gettysburg: From the Aftermath to the Address presented by Greg Caggiano Monday, November 16, 2026 at 7:00 PM Montclair Women’s Club 82 Union Street, Montclair NJ This venue is handicap accessible. Parking is available behind the building and on the street. Light refreshments, coffee and tea will be served. The program is free for members, and $10 for guests. In July 1863, Gettysburg had a population of 2,000 and was inundated with over 160,000 Union and Confederate soldiers. The largest battle of the war ravaged the town, leaving behind thousands of dead, farmlands turned red, and homes destroyed. item.title: NJ Death Cafe — Mon Nov 16, 7:00 PM — Cornerstone Montclair
item.description:
We invite you to join us for a Death Cafe in the garden. Seating will be provided, but feel free to bring a blanket if want to sit on the grass. This facilitated gathering allows for our community to come together to talk openly and honestly about life and death over refreshments. This is an open space to explore personal thoughts and feelings about death, ultimately helping people to live fuller lives. Participants are encouraged to share, listen, and contemplate mortality in a safe, confidential, and nonjudgmental environment. Everyone is welcome—all identities, experiences, and beliefs. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10:15 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*
